title: onprem: vendor offline bundle + add RKE2 / Rancher / Flatcar distro support
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: Vendor the on-prem/air-gapped offline bundle and add explicit support for RKE2, Rancher-managed clusters, and Flatcar nodes. This change updates the bundle builder, Helm overlays, Terraform inputs, and installer migration to improve compatibility for customers installing Redwood in strictly air-gapped or conservative distro environments. Motivation: Multiple enterprise customers and recent incident reports showed failures during offline installs due to missing distro-specific systemd/containerd overlays, mismatched image tags, and TLS registry bootstrapping gaps for Rancher/RKE2 and Flatcar. This PR vendors the exact images and artifacts we use in CI, adds distro overlays and initContainers for certificate bootstrapping, and exposes registry/registry-ca inputs for the installer and Terraform modules. What changed (high level): - offline-bundle: new vendor scripts and a reproducible bundle manifest (scripts/vendor_bundle.sh, scripts/generate-bundle-manifest.sh). Bundles now include all container images, OS packages (Flatcar), and Helm charts required for an install. - helm: added distro overlays under charts/onprem/distro-overlays/{rke2,rancher,flatcar}; new values for imagePullSecrets, registry.tlsCa, and initContainer for registry bootstrap. - installer: installer binary picks distro overlay automatically based on node-label detection and supports a --bundle=<path> flag for local bundle installs. - terraform: module redwood_onprem now accepts mirror_registry, registry_ca_pem, and skip_internet boolean to wire provider configs for air-gapped clusters. - security: signed bundle manifest verification (cosign) is integrated into the installer; added verification step to CI. - docs: updated docs/airgap.md with bundle generation and upgrade steps. Upgrade/migration notes: - Backward compatible: older bundles will continue to install if they include the legacy manifest format. - For customers upgrading from <2025.11 bundles, run: redwood-installer migrate-bundle --from <old-bundle> --to <new-bundle> to create a compatibility manifest. - If using Rancher-managed clusters, ensure the cluster's local registry has certs added to the node trust store; the installer will attempt to patch via initContainers when possible. Testing and validation: - Local airgap lab: validated install on RKE2 1.27 with Flatcar 3453 and Rancher v2.8-managed clusters. - CI: unit, integration, and an airgap e2e job using the new vendored bundle. Initial e2e failed due to missing ca cert handling; fixed in commit 3 and job re-run passed. - Manual verification: smoke test generated that validates image digests in the bundle manifest vs images pulled during install. Migration/rollout plan: - Merge to main and cut a patch release for private-installer 1.12.1. - Announce to SRE/customer success and include migration checklist in the release notes. - Recommend customers test in staging air-gapped environment before production rollout. Checklist: - [x] Vendor bundle generator and manifest - [x] Helm overlays and values - [x] Installer bundle flag and cosign verification - [x] Terraform inputs for offline registry - [x] Docs updated (airgap.md) - [x] QA e2e passing Notes: This PR vendors additional ~1.2k LOC of generated manifest data and image lists; core logic changes are limited to scripts, overlays, and installer wiring. If there are very large diffs to images they are included as manifest entries only (not raw blobs in the repo).

release_notes: Added on-prem/offline bundle vendor tooling and first-class support for RKE2, Rancher managed clusters, and Flatcar nodes in the private installer. Includes cosign verification for bundles, Terraform inputs for mirrored registries, and Helm distro overlays. See docs/airgap.md for upgrade and migration instructions.
notes_for_support: If customers report image digest mismatches after upgrade, ask for the bundle-manifest.json from the failed install and run scripts/verify-manifest.sh locally. If Rancher clusters fail due to local registry certs, ensure registry CA PEM is provided via Terraform input mirror_registry_ca and restart kubelet on nodes after cert injection.
